patients.summary: Healthy young woman who works at an artisan bakery and is on a university student plan; joined in 2022 with functional constipation managed on psyllium. Two uncomplicated cystitis episodes in 2025, each treated with nitrofurantoin; otherwise routine preventive care.

documents.title: New Patient Intake Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller: patient (Sophia Roy, DOB 11/20/2000).

Wants to establish with the practice. Has been seen at her previous primary care office since childhood and would like to move closer to where she lives and works now. Mentioned she has a university student health plan as primary and her parents' PPO as secondary - both cards to be scanned at the visit.

Scheduled new patient physical 9/8 at 8:30. Membership agreement and intake forms sent to portal. Records release signed electronically; request faxed to prior office for immunizations and last visit notes.

No current concerns per pt.

conditions.note: Longstanding per patient; manages with fiber as needed.

documents.title: New Patient Visit - Establish Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - ESTABLISHING CARE

21 y/o woman here to start with us. Grew up in the area, was followed at her previous primary care office until now. Works at an artisan bakery in town (early shifts) and is enrolled at the university, which is where her primary insurance comes from. Feels well. No acute concerns.

PMH: Constipation - functional, has had it for years. Goes a few days at a time without a BM when her schedule gets busy, otherwise fine. No blood, no weight loss, no night symptoms. Uses psyllium powder when she needs it, roughly a tablespoon in water, and that works for her. Never had a workup and never needed a prescription.
No other medical problems. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.

Meds: psyllium powder PRN. No prescription meds. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.

FH: Mom has had a lot of bladder infections over the years. Dad has high blood pressure. Nobody with kidney disease or kidney stones that she knows of.

SH: Lives in Holyoke. Bakery associate, student. Never smoked. Alcohol socially on weekends, a drink or two. Denies drug use.

ROS: Negative except as above. Periods regular.

Exam:
Vitals as recorded. BMI normal.
Gen: well-appearing, pleasant.
HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx without lesions. Neck supple, thyroid normal size, no lymphadenopathy.
CV: RRR, no murmur.
Lungs: CTA bilaterally.
Abd: soft, NT/ND, normal bowel sounds, no masses or HSM.
Ext: warm, no edema.
Skin: no rashes.
Neuro/psych: grossly nonfocal; mood and affect normal.

PHQ-2: 0. AUDIT-C: 2.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Health maintenance, new patient. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. HIV and hep C one-time screens offered and accepted. Tdap today - last one at 11 per her recollection, will confirm against outside records. Flu shot once supply is in, nurse visit next month. Cervical screening to start at her next physical.
2. Functional constipation - longstanding, no alarm features. TSH and calcium with today's labs. Keep using psyllium; talked about fluids and not putting off the bathroom on long shifts.

Return in 1 year for physical, sooner as needed. She has my cell for anything in between.

documents.title: Lab Results - New Patient Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Sophia,

All of your bloodwork from last week came back normal - blood counts, kidney and liver tests, calcium, thyroid and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screening tests were both negative. Nothing to change.

Talk soon,
Your primary care physician

documents.title: Records From Prior Primary Care Office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 9 pages. Scanned to media.

Summary entered by staff:
- Immunization record: childhood series complete (DTaP/IPV/Hib/HepB/MMR/varicella per the printout). Adolescent: Tdap and MenACWY 01/2012, MenACWY booster 03/2017, HPV quadrivalent x2 (01/2012, 08/2012). COVID-19 Pfizer primary series 04/2021 and 05/2021.
- Last well visit there 2021: well, constipation noted, fiber suggested.
- Allergies on their list: NKDA.
- No screening labs or Pap on file.

Immunizations abstracted to chart. Tdap date matches what pt told us - the 9/8 Tdap is the 10-year booster.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
In after her bakery shift for flu and COVID booster. Screening questions negative; no prior vaccine reactions. VIS/EUA fact sheet given.

Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid.
Pfizer bivalent booster 0.3 mL IM right deltoid.

Observed 15 min, tolerated well, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Constipation question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Quick question, not urgent. We've had a lot of long shifts at the bakery lately and I basically don't get a real break, so I've been going like 3-4 days without going. The psyllium still works when I take it but I keep forgetting until it's already bad. Is it ok to just take it every day? Or should I be doing something else?

documents.title: RE: Constipation question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sophia - yes, taking the psyllium every day during the busy stretches is completely fine, and honestly works better that way than waiting until you're backed up. Same dose, lots of water with it. A water bottle at your station helps, and try to give yourself a few minutes in the morning before your shift, since that's when the gut is most active. If you start having pain, blood, or it stops responding to the fiber, let me know and we'll take a closer look.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical.

S: Doing well. Still at the bakery, more hours this summer. Constipation better since she started taking the psyllium daily on heavy weeks - most weeks now regular. No other concerns. Sexually active; reviewed STI screening, agreeable. LMP 2 weeks ago, regular.
Meds: psyllium PRN/daily on busy weeks. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, a drink or two on weekends.

O: Vitals reviewed, normal.
General: well.
Neck: no thyromegaly or nodes.
Heart RRR without murmur; lungs clear.
Abdomen soft, nontender.
Pelvic: normal external genitalia; speculum exam with normal-appearing cervix, Pap collected. Tolerated with some nerves - first one, talked her through it.
Skin: no concerning lesions.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
- Health maintenance: first Pap today (age 22). Urine GC/CT. Tdap current (2022). Flu and COVID this fall, nurse visit.
- Functional constipation: stable on fiber.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Pap and STI screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sophia, your Pap came back normal, and the chlamydia and gonorrhea tests were negative. With a normal Pap at your age the next one is in 3 years (2026). Thanks for getting through the first one!

Flu quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, lot recorded.
COVID (Pfizer, updated) 0.3 mL IM R deltoid, lot recorded.
Waited 15 min, no issues.

documents.body: Hi, my university is asking for an updated immunization form before spring registration (they say they don't have my meningitis dates). I uploaded the form here. Can someone fill it out and sign it? Thank you!

documents.body: University immunization compliance form completed from chart immunization record (MenACWY 2012 and 2017, Tdap 2022, MMR/varicella/hep B series per prior office record). Signed by PCP. Uploaded back to portal and copy to media. Pt notified.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, age 23.

No complaints. Bowels okay - uses the psyllium on and off, more when work is hectic. Sleeping fine, mood good. Sexually active, wants the yearly STI urine test again.

Meds: psyllium powder as needed. NKDA.
Never smoker. Weekend drinks only, 1-2.

Plan:

- Pap last year normal - next due 2026.

See her next summer.

documents.title: Burning when I pee
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, since Sunday it burns every time I pee and I feel like I have to go constantly, plus kind of an ache low in my belly. No fever. I think it's a UTI? Can I be seen today? I'm off at 11.

documents.title: RN Triage - Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt back re: portal message. Dysuria, frequency and lower abdominal ache x2 days. Denies fever, back/flank pain, vaginal discharge or bleeding. Not pregnant to her knowledge. Tolerating fluids.
No red flags. Booked same-day with PCP at 11:40; asked her not to void right before arriving so we can get a clean-catch sample.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit - Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: burning with urination

HPI: 24F, two days of dysuria with frequency and a suprapubic ache. Started Sunday. No vaginal discharge, no vaginal bleeding. No fever, no back or flank pain. First time she's had this. One partner currently; condoms some of the time but not consistently.

PMH: functional constipation.
Meds: psyllium powder PRN. Since January also taking vitamin C 500 mg daily and a multivitamin with zinc daily - read about it for immune support during the winter.
NKDA.
FH notable for mom with recurrent UTIs; dad HTN; no kidney disease or stones in the family.

Exam: Vitals WNL, afebrile.
Uncomfortable but well-appearing.
Abd: mild tenderness over the suprapubic area. No rebound, no guarding. No CVA tenderness.
Pelvic: offered, she is not comfortable with it today - deferred.

Clean-catch UA (in office): LE positive, nitrite positive, WBC >10/hpf, RBC 0-2/hpf, many gram-negative rods.
Urine hCG negative.

A/P:
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis. Classic symptoms, positive dip and micro, no upper tract features. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5 days. Push fluids.
2. Sexually active, under 25, inconsistent condoms - urine GC/CT sent since she declined the pelvic. Will message results.
3. Supplements noted and added to med list.

If fever, back pain, vomiting, or not better in 48 h, call or text me.

documents.title: STI test results

documents.body: Sophia - chlamydia and gonorrhea tests from Tuesday were negative. How are the bladder symptoms doing?

documents.title: RE: STI test results

documents.title: RE: STI test results

documents.body: Great, glad it cleared. Reach out if it comes back.

Med rec: psyllium PRN; vitamin C 500 mg daily; multivitamin with zinc daily. No Rx meds. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks on weekends.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

- Hx cystitis x1: no recurrence.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit - Recurrent Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: dysuria again

HPI: 24F with functional constipation and one prior cystitis (Feb 2025) back with 3 days of painful urination, urgency and discomfort above the pubic bone - says it feels just like February. No fever or chills. No flank pain. No vaginal discharge.
ROS otherwise negative: no nausea or vomiting, no back pain, no vaginal irritation, no abnormal bleeding. Hasn't been sick recently. Got her flu shot at a vaccine day through her university last month (mid-September).
Bowels: still has the occasional mild constipation when breaks at work are irregular - she's full-time at the bakery now - but nothing different lately.

Meds: psyllium PRN, multivitamin with zinc daily. Stopped the vitamin C recently. No prescription meds.
NKDA.
SH: never smoker, social drinker. One partner for the last four months.
FH: mother with recurrent UTIs; father HTN; no renal disease/stones.

Exam: T 37.1, BP 112/72, P 82.
NAD. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, otherwise nontender, no CVA tenderness. Rest of exam unremarkable.

UA dip: LE positive, nitrite positive. Urine hCG negative.

A/P:
1. Acute cystitis, second episode in 8 months. Uncomplicated - afebrile, no flank pain. Urine culture sent this time. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5 days again, worked well last time. Will adjust if culture says otherwise.
2. New partner since summer, under 25 - urine GC/CT added.
3. Med list updated: vitamin C off.
4. Flu 9/2025 recorded from patient report.

Return precautions reviewed. Message me in a few days with how she's doing.

documents.title: Immunization History Updated
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Per patient at today's visit: influenza vaccine received 9/18/2025 at a university vaccination event. Product and lot not known to patient. Entered as historical; state registry query shows a 2025-26 influenza dose on that date.

documents.title: Urine culture and STI results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sophia - your urine culture grew E. coli, the usual bladder-infection bacteria, and it is sensitive to the nitrofurantoin you're taking, so finish the course as planned. Chlamydia and gonorrhea were negative.

documents.title: Feeling better
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the antibiotic today, everything's back to normal. Is there anything I can do so this doesn't keep happening? My mom used to get these all the time.

documents.title: RE: Feeling better
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you're better. Two in a year is common and doesn't mean anything is wrong. The things with the best track record are simple: drink plenty of water through the day (hard at work, I know), don't hold it for long stretches, and pee soon after sex. Keeping the constipation under control helps too. If you get a third one within a year we'd talk about other options, so let me know.

documents.title: New insurance card
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the student health plan sent new cards for the spring semester (same plan, new member number). Pictures of front and back attached. My parents' PPO is the same as before.

documents.title: Insurance updated
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Primary coverage updated with new student plan member ID from uploaded card images. Secondary (parental PPO) unchanged. Eligibility verified.

documents.title: Cranberry pills?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Random question - my mom swears by cranberry pills for bladder infections. Since I've had two, should I be taking them? No symptoms right now, just wondering.

documents.title: RE: Cranberry pills?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. The research on cranberry is mixed - some studies show a small benefit for women who get frequent infections, others show nothing. You've had two, months apart, and you're doing all the right things, so I wouldn't push it. If you want to try it, it's very unlikely to hurt, but let me know so I can put it on your list. The water and voiding habits matter more.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 25 y/o.

Feeling well. No urinary symptoms since last October - two cystitis episodes total (2/2025, 10/2025), both nitrofurantoin-responsive, culture last time E. coli. Didn't start cranberry. Constipation quiet; psyllium a few times a month. Still full-time at the bakery.

Meds: psyllium PRN, multivitamin with zinc daily. NKDA.
Never smoker; 1-2 drinks on weekends.

Exam: vitals normal. Well-appearing young woman. HEENT clear. Neck without adenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular rate and rhythm. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin without lesions of concern.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
- Cervical screening due (Pap 8/2023 normal). She'd rather not do it today - prefers a dedicated visit; will book for September and do her flu shot then.
- Labs: CBC/CMP normal last summer; nothing needed this year.
- Functional constipation: stable.
- Hx cystitis x2: no recurrence. Reviewed prevention habits.
Next physical summer 2027.
